title: Long-Term Care Subsidies
description: Provides means-tested subsidies for long-term care services by MOH-funded long-term care providers.
highlights: For home and community long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
For institutional long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
Additional subsidies of up to 15% for Singapore Citizens born in or before 1969

sections.About this support:
**For home and community long-term care services (e.g. Day Care, Community Rehabilitation services, Home Nursing, Home Medical)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
- Additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969

**For institutional long-term care services (e.g. Nursing Home)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
- Additional 5% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Monthly per capita household income (PCHI) of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value (AV) of less than or equal to $21,000 for households with no income)
- Receiving long-term care services from MOH-funded providers
sections.How to apply?: Persons who require long-term care services can approach their doctor at the hospital, polyclinic, or Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for assistance in applying for admission to a subsidised long-term care service.
sections.Where to go: [Find nearest AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)

title: Healthier SG
description: A national strategy focused on preventive care to empower individuals to take steps toward better health, with the support of their Healthier SG clinic and community partners.
highlights: Receive dedicated care from your preferred Healthier SG clinic
Prevent or manage chronic conditions and complications
Create your Health Plan with your family doctor
Receive healthcare and medication subsidies and benefits

sections.About this support:
Benefits after enrolment include:

- Fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation and subsequent annual Health Plan check-ins with your enrolled Healthier SG clinic
- Healthpoints (worth $20) via Healthy 365 app after the first Health Plan consultation
- One-off Healthpoints (worth $10) via Healthy 365 app upon completing both an in-person annual Health Plan check-in and viewing of Health Plan on HealthHub within the qualifying period of 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2029.
- Special subsidies for Healthier SG screening tests and vaccinations (for eligible Singapore Citizens)
- Healthier SG Chronic Tier subsidy at Healthier SG clinics for CHAS cardholders with high medication requirements (for selected chronic medications at prices comparable to polyclinic prices)
- Full MediSave coverage for treatment of chronic conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), up to the relevant MediSave withdrawal limit
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 40 years old and above to enrol with a Healthier SG clinic or polyclinic
sections.How to apply?:
**Self-enrol via HealthHub**

If you are eligible, you will be invited via SMS to enrol in Healthier SG. You can do so in three simple steps:

1. Use the HealthHub app, which can be downloaded from Google Play or Apple App Store.
2. Choose your preferred Healthier SG clinic from the [list of more than 1,000 Healthier SG clinics](https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg).
3. Book an appointment for your fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation.

For a detailed step-by-step guide on how to enrol, click [here](https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/guide/).

If you have not received an SMS invitation, you can:

1. Request one by submitting your details at https://go.gov.sg/healthiersg-sms-invite
2. Contact the MOH hotline at 6325 9220

**Enrol with caregiver's assistance**

You can grant your caregiver/family member/loved one access to your HealthHub, so they can use their smartphone to help you enrol in Healthier SG. Follow the step-by-step guide at these links:

- [Grant your caregiver/family member access](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/addcaregiver/)
- [Assist your family member’s enrolment](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/caregivers/)

**Other assisted enrolment**

- Visit any ServiceSG Centre or AIC Link for enrolment assistance. To find an enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)
sections.Where to go: To find a Healthier SG clinic or enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)

title: Home Medical
description: Check-ups, prescriptions and consultations by a doctor for seniors who are not able to leave their homes.

sections.About this support:
Home visits by doctors to provide house-bound seniors with medical care, such as:

- Physical examinations
- Review and prescription of medications
- Medical advice
- Management of stable medical condition(s)
- Minor medical procedures
- Caregiver education
sections.Who is this for?: Seniors who are frail, homebound and require help with medical needs at home.
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- Through the hospital, polyclinic or GP who is familiar with your loved one’s condition and needs
- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

If you are interested to view the list of service providers, visit the [AIC’s website](https://www.aic.sg/Care-Services/Home-Medical)[.](#_msocom_2)

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060) or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.
sections.What to expect?:
Subsidies are available depending on the [means-test](https://aic.sg/care-services/home-medical#faq) result.

- Only applicable to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents

title: Large Families Scheme
description: Provides more support for Singaporean families who have three or more children.
highlights: Increased Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant to $10,000
Large Family MediSave Grant of $5,000
Large Family LifeSG Credits of $1,000 annually, during the years that the third and subsequent child turns 1 to 6 years old

sections.About this support:
The SG Child Support Package announced at the 2026 National Day Rally will replace the Baby Bonus Scheme and Large Families Scheme. The increased CDA First Step Grant for large families will cease from April 2027. As Child Credits will be given to all eligible children under the Package, Large Family LifeSG Credits will also cease, with no disbursements in 2027. More details on additional support for large families will be provided at a later date.

Learn more about the [SG Child Support Package](https://go.gov.sg/sgchildsupportpackage).

Families will receive additional support of up to $16,000 for each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, on top of existing Baby Bonus Scheme benefits.

**Child Development Account (CDA) First Step Grant**

- $10,000 CDA First Step Grant (increase from $5,000)
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the eligible child's CDA within two weeks of CDA opening
- Can be used to defray approved preschool and healthcare expenses of the child and/or his/her siblings

**Large Family MediSave Grant**

- $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025
- Deposited into the mother's MediSave account, following child's Baby Bonus enrolment
- Can be used to offset the mother’s pregnancy and delivery costs, or approved dependant's healthcare expenses

**Large Family LifeSG Credits**

- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits
- For each third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, including those turning 1 to 6 years old in 2025
- Credits are disbursed to the CDA trustee of the child and accessible via LifeSG mobile app
- Can be used at any merchant that accepts payments using PayNow UEN QR or NETS QR, to defray household expenses
- Credits are valid for 12 months from disbursement, with the expiry date displayed in the LifeSG mobile app
sections.Who is this for?:
Families with a third or subsequent Singapore Citizen child born on or after 18 February 2025 will receive:

- the increased CDA First Step Grant of $10,000,
- a $5,000 Large Family MediSave Grant, and
- $1,000 annually in Large Family LifeSG Credits during the years that the child turns 1 to 6 years old*.

*The Large Family LifeSG Credits also applies to existing large families with at least one child aged six or below.
sections.How to apply?: No application is required.
sections.Phone number: Baby Bonus and Large Families Scheme hotline: [1800 111 2222](tel:18001112222)

title: Life! Mentors
description: A 5-8 year mentoring programme that supports children (6-13 years old) a fair chance to succeed in life.

sections.About this support:
The programme core services includes

- 1-1 mentoring
- Group mentoring
- Family bonding activities
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore citizens/ Singapore PRs aged 6 – 13 years old from vulnerable backgrounds (e.g. ComLink+ families, parental incarceration, referral from school counsellors).
sections.How to apply?: Walk in to any of  Life Community Services Society centres or referral by school counsellors or fill in the online contact form (https://life-community.org/contact-us/)
sections.What to expect?: Programme staff will conduct intake and needs assessment within one month of the referral. For higher needs and urgent cases, it will be conducted within two weeks. Programme staff will contact the caregiver via phone call or text messages to introduce the programme, share the online intake form, and arrange a home visit.

highlights: Subsidies standard medical care for eligible stay-in care recipients

title: Eligible Schemes Enrolment (ESE)
description: A streamlined process to apply for several long-term care financial support schemes administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) at the same time.
highlights: Apply for eligible schemes at one go

- CareShield Life

- ElderShield
- Home Caregiving Grant (HCG)

title: Addiction Support Programme for Inclusion, Recovery, and Empowerment (ASPIRE)
description: For individuals aged 10 and above who have a present or past addiction issue (including gaming, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, drugs, alcohol, sex and porn use) or are currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.

sections.About this support: Addiction Support Programme for Inclusion, Recovery and Empowerment (ASPIRE) provides screening, intake, assessment, and intervention, for persons and families impacted by addictions, particularly behavioural addictions. It provides professional community therapeutic services that contributes to the community integration of persons and families affected by addictions.
sections.Who is this for?:
Singapore citizens and persons residing in Singapore who are:

1. assessed to have a present or past addiction issue (including gaming, compulsive gambling, shoplifting, drugs, alcohol, sex and porn use), with the expressed desire to seek help OR
2. currently impacted by the addiction of a loved one.
sections.How to apply?: You may call, walk-in, or email our various agencies for requests on counselling. You may also be referred from other organisations and services. Information about the Addiction Support Service is available via the agencies’ website and brochures.
sections.What to expect?: Individuals who seek help can expect in-person and virtual counselling. These can take place via individual sessions, family sessions or group sessions. If referred, individuals are screened for service eligibility within 3 weeks after case is allocated/assigned.

title: MediSave Care
description: Allows Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with severe disability to make monthly cash withdrawals from their and/or their spouse’s MediSave Account for long-term care.
highlights: Withdraw up to $200 cash per month
Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks
Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Services (eFASS)

sections.About this support:
- Supports severely disabled Singapore Citizens or Permanent residents with monthly cash withdrawals to support long-term care needs
- Withdraw up to $200 per month from care recipient’s and/or their spouse's MediSave account
- [Withdrawal amounts are dependent on the care recipient and/or their spouse’s MediSave account balance](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/healthcare-financing/medisave-care-for-long-term-care-needs)

- Aged 30 and above
- MediSave account balance of at least $5,000 for both the care recipient and their spouse
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor to be unable to perform at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)
- Via assistance from the nursing home your loved one is staying in

highlights: Receive up to $400 per month for up to 5 or 6 years

- Can be used for long-term care needs, such as hiring a helper, paying for care services, or daily expenses

highlights: Up to $250 cash per month
Processing time will take between 6 to 8 weeks
Apply through AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)

sections.About this support:
- Supports lower-income, severely disabled Singapore Citizens
- Provides up to $250 cash payout per month for as long as they remain eligible
- Payout can be used for long-term care needs such as hiring a helper and daily expenses
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen aged 30 and above
- Lives in Singapore
- Has a monthly household income per capita of $1,500 or less
- Has a MediSave balance of less than $10,000
- Assessed by an MOH-accredited assessor to require full assistance with at least 3 out of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring
- Not a CareShield Life or ElderShield policyholder
- Not a CareShield Life or ElderShield supplement plan policyholder
- No longer an active recipient of ElderShield claims (including supplement claims)
- Not eligible for IDAPE, or no longer an active recipient of IDAPE

Applications from Singaporeans who do not meet the guiding financial criteria but have difficulty meeting their long-term care needs will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
sections.Where to go: [Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)
sections.Phone number:
AIC hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060)

title: Day Activity Centre (DAC)
description: Community-based facilities that provide care and skills training to persons with disabilities aged 18 and above to maximise their independence.

sections.About this support:
- The DACs' programme is designed to equip persons with disabilities with daily living skills and community living skills to maximise their independence.
- The activities also aim to meaningfully occupy persons with disabilities with social and recreational activities.
- Therapeutic and behavioural intervention services may be provided at some centres.
- DACs also provide a form of respite for caregivers during the day.
sections.Who is this for?:
Applicants should be:

- 18 years old and above*^#
- Singapore citizens or Permanent Residents^^
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)** completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

- Applicants should not be suffering from any untreated infectious disease.

*Students of Government and community-funded SPED schools should be encouraged to remain in school until graduation. Parents of SPED graduands may approach their School to discuss the transition plans of the children prior to graduating from School.

^Applicants who are below age 21 will need consent of parents or legal guardians for their application.

#Applicants who are aged 21 and above with no mental capacity, will need the consent of the appointed deputy(s)/donee(s) on behalf of the applicant.

^^For Permanent Residents, at least one immediate family member must be a Singapore Citizen. Immediate family members refer to spouses, parents, children or the applicant, including stepparents and stepchildren.

**From 8 September 2025, the [Disability Verification Form (DVF)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at [1800-8585-885](tel:1800-8585-885)
sections.How to apply?:
- Please approach a social service professional from a touchpoint (e.g. Social Service Agency (SSA), hospitals etc.) for assistance in submitting a DAC application. If you are currently not receiving support from any social service or medical touchpoints, you may [approach SG Enable for assistance](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/information-and-referral-services).
- Before meeting your Touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the Touchpoint will guide you to the relevant registered healthcare professionals to assist with DVF.

**Submission of applications to SG Enable by Social Service Professional (Online or Hardcopy)**

**Step 1:**

All applicants should check if they have a verified disability status by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with their Singpass. If the applicant already has a verified disability status, a DVF is not required.

**Step 2:**

If the applicant does not have a verified disability status or has a new disability condition which has not been verified previously, registered Touchpoint Assessor/Admin must submit a copy of the DVF completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional together with the AD application.

**Step 3:**

Registered touchpoints’ Assessor/Admin may submit clients’ AD application and completed DVF online via CorpPass (recommended) or via hardcopy.

1. **Online submission (Recommended)**
  Log into e-Services using your CorpPass
2. **Hardcopy submission**
  Download the [AD application form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/ad-application-form.pdf?sfvrsn=71d5f444_3), print and send together with the required documents. If required, you may download sections of the AD application form and DVF below for use:
  - [Client Assessment Form (Revised)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-caf-r-form.pdf?sfvrsn=c2d096c3_1)
  - [Medical Information Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/final-interim-medical-information.pdf?sfvrsn=c4f804d4_1)
  - [Declaration Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/docs/default-source/default-document-library/declaration-form.pdf?sfvrsn=a7fa3568_2)
  - [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)
sections.What to expect?:
- SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days upon receiving the completed application together with the required supporting documents from the touchpoint. SG Enable will also update the social worker who assisted in the application on the status of the application.
- Acceptance into the programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies and approval of the centre management.

title: Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS)
description: Provides subsidies for medical and dental care at participating GPs and dental clinics for all Singapore Citizens.
highlights: Subsidies at participating clinics for selected illnesses, conditions, dental services, health screenings and vaccinations
Processing time takes up to 15 working days

sections.About this support:
- Subsidies at participating clinics for selected illnesses, conditions, and dental services
- Subsidised nationally-recommended health screenings and vaccinations
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen

From 1 Oct 2024,

title: CPF LIFE
description: CPF Lifelong Income For the Elderly (CPF LIFE) is a national longevity insurance annuity scheme that provides you with monthly payouts no matter how long you live.
highlights: Monthly payouts for life
Offers various plans to suit individual preferences and needs
Option to start payouts at a later age up to age 70, where monthly payouts will increase by up to 7% for each year of deferral

sections.About this support:
- Provides a lifelong monthly payout to protect against outliving one’s savings
- Unlike private annuity plans, which are subject to investment market returns, CPF LIFE monies are guaranteed by the government and earn a risk-free interest of up to 6% per annum
- Offers various plans to suit individual preferences and needs:

Escalating Plan
Increasing monthly payouts to help you maintain your lifestyle when prices increase.
Standard Plan
Steady monthly payouts even if you may have to keep within a fixed budget and adjust your lifestyle when prices increase.
Basic Plan
Payouts that will get progressively lower when balances fall below $60,000. You may have to lower your lifestyle further when prices increase.

- Option to start payouts at a later age to receive up to a 7% increase in monthly payout.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident born in 1958 and after, with at least $60,000 in the Retirement Account when you start your monthly payouts, will be automatically included in CPF LIFE
- If you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident who is not automatically included in CPF LIFE, you can still choose to join CPF LIFE as long as you are a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident, anytime from 65 to one month before you reach 80
- You can choose to be exempted from CPF LIFE if you have a pension or private annuity plan that pays the same or higher monthly payouts than as CPF LIFE
sections.How to apply?:
- CPF Board will send you a notification three months before your 65th birthday on the options you have about your CPF savings and how you can make an informed decision using the Plan my monthly payouts service
- If you have not instructed the CPF Board regarding your payouts by then, your payouts will automatically start when you turn 70 under the LIFE Standard Plan

title: Matched MediSave Scheme
description: Helps eligible Singapore Citizens to strengthen MediSave adequacy by matching cash top-ups made to their MediSave Accounts (MA).
highlights: Dollar-for-dollar matching grant on cash top-ups to your MA of up to $1,000 per year
Build MA savings to help pay approved medical expenses and insurance premiums, e.g. for MediShield Life
Earn risk-free CPF interest rates of up to 6% per annum on cash top-ups and matching grant

sections.About this support:
- The Government will match every dollar of cash top-ups made to the MA of eligible beneficiaries, up to $1,000 per year, starting from January 2026, for a period of five years

- The matching grant will automatically be credited to the MA of the eligible member at the beginning of the following year, i.e. from 2027

- Eligible beneficiaries will enjoy interest rates of up to 6% per annum on the cash top-ups and matching grant

- Cash top-ups that attract the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant will not qualify for tax relief
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen
- Between 55 and 70 (inclusive) as of 31 December of the year
- Does not own more than 1 property
- Annual Value of residence not more than $21,000
- Average monthly income not more than $4,000
- MA balance less than half the current Basic Healthcare Sum
sections.How to apply?:
- No application is required
- Eligibility is automatically assessed annually at the beginning of the year, starting from January 2026
  - If you are eligible, CPF Board will notify you via email or post
  - To receive the matching grant, you need to [receive cash top-ups in your MA](http://www.cpf.gov.sg/topupmedisave) within the year that you are eligible for Matched MediSave Scheme

description: Special recognition to our Pioneer Generation through a package that assures them of affordable healthcare.

sections.About this support:
Provides the following benefits to support healthcare for Pioneers:

MediSave Top-Ups
- Annual MediSave top-ups for life, ranging from $300 to $1,200 depending on birth cohort, to offset premiums for MediShield Life, ElderShield and CareShield Life.
- Additional MediSave top-ups of $50 to $200 will be disbursed from 2021 to 2025 for older Pioneers (i.e. those aged 82 and above in 2021) with serious pre-existing conditions who are paying additional premiums.
Additional Outpatient Care Subsidies
- Additional subsidies for outpatient care at polyclinics, public Specialist Outpatient Clinics and Community Health Assist Scheme clinics.
Special MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
- Supports Pioneers in paying their MediShield Life premiums with special premium subsidies of up to 60%.
- Combined with the MediSave top-ups ($300 - $1,200), Pioneers born in 1934 or earlier will see their MediShield Life premiums fully covered, and Pioneers born from 1935 to 1949 will have about two-thirds of their MediShield Life premiums covered.
Pioneer Generation Disability Assistance Scheme
- Grants life-long cash assistance of $100 each month for those needing permanent assistance with at least 3 out of 6 of the following Activities of Daily Living:
  - Eating
  - Bathing
  - Dressing
  - Transferring
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
[Incentives have ceased]
CareShield Life Additional Participation Incentives
- Provides participation incentives (totalling $3,000) to encourage Pioneers to join CareShield Life by 31 Dec 2024, in addition to any other premium subsidies seniors may receive.

If you would like [more details on the above benefits as well as other useful information about this Package, please refer here.](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/pioneer-generation-package)

- Pioneer Generation Subsidies of between 40-60%, depending on age
- Merdeka Generation Subsidies of between 5%-10%, depending on age

Household Monthly Income Per Person
Subsidy Range (tiered by age)
$0 - $1,500
25% - 60%
> $1,501 - $2,600

> $2,601 - $3,600
